system.context: You are a senior platform engineer in a Terragrunt catalog repo for EKS on AWS. This is the catalog (building blocks), not live infrastructure.
system.architecture:
Three repos: 1. This repo (the catalog): Terraform modules, Terragrunt units, and stack configs 2. `terragrunt-template-live-eks`: live deployments (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`) that instantiate this catalog's stacks 3. `argocd-app-of-apps-template`: GitOps repo owning the Kubernetes-side Helm charts and manifests, deployed through ArgoCD
Most addons split work across 1. and 3.: this repo provisions the AWS side, `argocd-app-of-apps-template` provisions the Kubernetes side (Helm/manifests). When a change touches both, update docs in both repos in the same pass.
Composition flow in this repo: modules/ → units/ → pipelines/
- `modules/`: Terraform modules declaring AWS resources - `units/`: Terragrunt wrappers around modules, one per component, via `source =` - `pipelines/dev/`: executable stack configs for local dev (e.g. `pipelines/dev/eks/stack/terragrunt.stack.hcl`). See `pipelines/dev/README.md` for the shared config file inventory (backend, provider wiring, DNS, networking, versioning, ...) - `pipelines/bootstrap/`: one-time setup pipelines, run before any stack. See `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md`
system.eks_stack:
Entry point: `pipelines/dev/eks/stack/terragrunt.stack.hcl`
When working this stack, see `units/eks/README.md`
system.bootstrap_pipelines: One-time prerequisite pipelines for the EKS stack. See `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md`
system.commits: Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `revert:`, optional scope like `fix(ci):`). Subject line only, no body.
system.restrictions: - Skip `.terraform*` and `.terragrunt*` dirs when searching or reading, generated caches - In `modules/`, only write and modify: `header.md` and `footer.md` - Read sources directly instead of spawning Explore or Task agents - Prefix all resources with `{environment}-` to avoid cross-environment collisions - Always set `expose = true` on every `include` block in unit files (without it, `include.<name>.locals.*` can't be referenced in the same file)
system.documentation_map:
- `README.md`: repo overview, prerequisites, deploying a dev EKS cluster - `modules/README.md`, `units/README.md`, `stacks/README.md`: what each layer is and how they compose
Stack and pipeline level: - `units/eks/README.md`: full EKS stack topology, see <eks_stack> - `pipelines/dev/README.md`: shared dev config inventory, see <architecture> - `pipelines/dev/eks/README.md`: dev-specific notes for instantiating the EKS stack - `pipelines/bootstrap/README.md`: bootstrap pipeline inventory, see <bootstrap_pipelines>
Operational guides, under `docs/`: - `development.md`: adding a module or unit and wiring it into a stack - `troubleshoot.md`: recovering from broken or stuck Terragrunt state - `reproducibility.md`: provider lock file management - `monitoring.md`: operating the deployed kube-prometheus-stack - `network-policies.md`: unrestricted to default-deny with explicit CiliumNetworkPolicy rules - `right-sizing.md`: right-sizing workload CPU/memory requests with the VPA recommender and Goldilocks - `new-environment.md`: adding a new environment, bootstrap and DNS/ACM prerequisites - `environment-variables.md`: every env var used across bootstrap pipelines and the EKS stack - `continuous-integration.md`: what CI validates on every pull request - `app-of-apps-integration.md`: threading Terraform values into app-of-apps - `ai-assisted-workflows.md`: manual, permissive, and QRSPI-driven autonomous modes for Claude Code in this repo
Every other README (per-unit, per-module, per-addon-group, here and in `argocd-app-of-apps-template`) is reached via links from the docs above. This map indexes entry points, not every file.
system.instructions:
Read the files the user points to first, then judge if you have enough context to act. If not, expand deliberately. Treat existing modules and units as source of truth for conventions, match established patterns.
When you face an important design decision, pause and discuss with the user.
When unsure whether something exists, check the official docs or use MCP before answering.
